long_biography.plain_text:
Chelsea's former Essoldo cinema became a redevelopment project for property entrepreneur Howard Raymond and his cousin Mark Quinn. The scheme combined a new cinema with shops, a restaurant and apartments. Its engineers had to separate noise between the cinema and adjoining homes while leaving room for ventilation within the building's restricted floor heights.

Raymond also co-founded The King of Soho drinks brand with Alex Robson. They sketched their business plan on a cocktail napkin and developed a citrus-led gin with grapefruit as a prominent flavour. Robson took responsibility for daily management, while Raymond contributed to the product's identity and its celebration of the district's entertainment history.
